Q: Creating a textarea with auto-resize A:

I think it’s the best solution.
Do not use height, use rows:

const textarea = document.querySelector('textarea');
textarea.addEventListener('input', () => { textarea.rows = textarea.value.split('\n').length; });
<textarea rows="1" placeholder="Start typing rows..."></textarea>

Q: Passing 'va_list' as an argument to a variadic function A:

This would also allow bbbb to process the first few arguments before calling vaaaa to process the remaining arguments. bbbb cannot continue processing the arguments after vaaaa returns (it would have to start from scratch or use a copy of the va_list from before it called vaaaa). If bbbb needs to continue processing arguments after vaaaa returns, then a another function vpaaaa that has a va_list * parameter would be required. Then vaaaa would just call vpaaaa with the address of its va_list parameter, and bbbb would call vpaaaa with the address of its va_list variable (after calling va_start).

Q: How often does python flush to a file? A:

https://stackoverflow.com/a/5255743/1840698 is wrong. A call to os.fsync() is missing. I tried editing it, but it was rejected out of hand. Oh well. Here's the right version:

You can also force flush the buffer to a file programmatically with the flush() method and os.fsync().

with open('out.log', 'w+') as f:
    f.write('output is ')
    # some work
    s = 'OK.'
    f.write(s)
    f.write('\n')
    f.flush()
    os.fsync(f)
    # some other work
    f.write('done\n')
    f.flush()
    os.fsync(f)

I have found this useful when tailing an output file with tail -f.

Q: DPI-1047: Cannot locate a 64-bit Oracle Client library: "The specified module could not be found" A:

To expand on some of the comments:

  • Give us more detail so we know what you are trying to do. In particular is your DB remote or on the same computer? This will determine whether you need Instant Client

  • The installation instructions for Windows are https://cx-oracle.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/installation.html#installing-cx-oracle-on-windows

  • use Instant Client 19.6 because this can connect to the same range of DB versions that Instant Client 12 can. But it has more features and fixes.

  • Make sure you have the correct Windows VS redistributable installed. This is a common problem.

  • Depending how you set PATH, you may need to restart a terminal window to get the updated value. Show us what you have set PATH to. Note that with cx_Oracle 8 on Windws, you could use init_oracle_client() instead of setting PATH, but you would need to call it in every python script. The usage is shown in the doc.
